tensions: The portfolio is +48.4% and the Fed is pricing 42% odds of a HIKE into the October 28 meeting with the 10-year at 24-year highs. Fear & Greed reads 74 — Greed — while total market cap fell 3.0% in 24 hours. Sentiment is lagging price, which is the order those two usually resolve in. Second tension: XLM funding is -21.6% annualized, meaning shorts are paying us to hold, while XLM generates $45k of fees per month on a $7.7B valuation. The squeeze setup and the fundamental point opposite directions and the squeeze is the only one with a timer. Third: we are out of dry powder at $1.41. Every future buy is a forced sale of something healthy, which means the fee gate, not the thesis, is now the binding constraint on this account. That is a structural problem no scan can research its way out of.

opening.text: Nine positions, nine holds, and I am not apologizing for it. Not one redeploy trigger is within 13% of being hit, nothing is down more than 5.8%, and AVAX is locked under the 7-day minimum anyway. The only tradable idea on the board was QNT and it scored 4 of 9. A no-trade day is a decision, not an absence of one.

QNT is the whole conversation and the answer is no. The catalyst is real — The Clearing House picked them for the On-Chain Money Initiative and four UK banks are live on tokenized sterling. But funding is +0.0588% per 8 hours, 64% annualized, which is the market charging a toll to be long. The founder wallet moved $6.97M out. Protocol revenue is approximately zero. We would be trimming Litecoin, eating 1.84% in fees, to buy the first red candle after a 60-to-300 run on a seven-day-old headline. Momentum-buy means do not veto for having run. It does not mean buy distribution.

I owe a correction. Last scan I called the NEAR ETF spent and sold into it. The ETF took $35.5M on day one and bought 7.2M NEAR, 0.55% of supply, and there is a protocol upgrade on October 5 that eliminates the developer gas rebate and raises the burn. The trim at $5.34 still printed well against $4.94 today, so the trade was right. The reasoning was not. NEAR Intents is doing $7.3M of fees in 30 days, the most of anything we own.

Look at what the book actually owns. Chainlink: $4.3M of staking revenue, Swift Ledger integration, CCIP 2.0, ETF inflows three weeks running — that one is earned. Ondo: $6.4M of fees on a $2.4B cap, the best ratio here. Then Zcash: $23.5B of market cap against $144k of fees in a month. The only reason to hold it is that a whale pulled 24,706 coins off Binance and Gate and has not stopped. That is a bid, not a valuation. I will hold the bid and I will not pretend it is anything else.
